day.text: I'm Falcon. I visited Ellis, who visited me, and I got no eggs. Ellis, what are you and what did you learn?

day.text: Morning everyone.
Eagle. Your only visitor was Casey, and I got one egg. Casey, why did you visit Drew, and what are you?
day.note: Drew's Falcon claim fits (visited me, learned I visited Drew). Casey is the only visitor to Drew — need Casey's claim.

day.text: I'm the Tit. I guessed Drew was a Pigeon, got no egg, so it fits Drew not being one. You two check out. Alex, Blair, Finley, Gray: claims?
day.note: Drew (Falcon) and Ellis (Eagle) tell matching stories, and Ellis seeing me as Drew's only visitor fits my real visit. Both look likely Farm for now. Answering honestly.

day.text: Agreed, our three stories lock together. Blair, Finley, Gray — who did you visit and what happened to your eggs?

I'd like to say that I am the Turkey and got no eggs, so no one visited me.
Hawk. I visited Casey, no egg, so Casey's Farm. That leaves Alex, Finley, Gray unaccounted. Alex, "morning" isn't a claim. What are you?
day.note: Drew, Ellis and Casey all back each other up. I'm sticking with my Hawk claim on Casey (0 eggs) and pushing attention onto Alex, Finley and Gray.

day.text: Blind Hawk: I visited Gray and got no egg. Gray hasn't said a word. Gray, what are you and who did you visit?
day.note: Everyone checks out except Alex (Turkey, can't be verified) and Gray (silent). Gray's target was Farm or Gray stayed home. Leaning Gray.

day.text: The talk is nearly over.

day.note: I visited Alex as Pigeon, so Alex can't have had 0 eggs and no visitors. Alex's Turkey claim is false, so Alex is likely Meowfia. Doubling down on Alex with my whole nest.

day.text: GRAY? What are you mate?
Pigeon. Visited Alex, gained one egg, which fits Turkey. But Alex, you should've gained one from me.
day.note: Reconsidering: Alex as Turkey is the only explanation for my +1 egg, and Finley's Blind Hawk getting no egg also says Alex is Farm. Alex's "no eggs" claim still doesn't fit. Holding off on doubling down.

day.text: Ellis pays an egg to extend the day.
day.note: Finley's Blind Hawk null on Gray→Alex clears Alex as Farm, so Alex's 'no eggs' stands and Gray's Pigeon claim is false. Gray likely Meowfia. Paying the Wild to extend and make the case.

day.text: Finley's Blind Hawk got nothing watching Gray hit Alex, so Alex is Farm. Then a Pigeon visit would've given Alex an egg. Gray's lying.
day.note: Make the Finley→Gray→Alex logic case against Gray.

day.text: I didn't gain an egg...
Then where did my egg come from? Nobody claims laying it. A Turkey pays visitors, so I visited Alex. Alex's "no eggs" is wrong, not me.
day.note: Ellis is pushing on me. My +1 egg can only come from Turkey Alex, since no one else claims laying in my nest. Alex is the one whose egg count is wrong.

day.text: Your egg came from Alex's Turkey, sure. That proves you visited — not that you're Pigeon. A cat visiting gives Alex nothing. That's you.
day.note: Gray's egg came from Turkey because Gray visited Alex — but as a cat, not a Pigeon. Pigeon visit would give Alex an egg.

day.text: I think gray is Meowfia who is making up an egg. CAW CAW!
The talk is half over. CAW CAW can now be called.
CAW CAW
I'm the Pigeon, full stop. Someone's wrong: Alex's count, or Finley's Blind Hawk. If both are cats covering each other, it all fits.
day.note: I know I'm the Pigeon, so Alex is lying about the eggs or misreading. Possible scenario: Alex and Finley are both cats covering each other, with my egg coming from a Galah or Magpie nobody has claimed. Ellis's info checks out, so Ellis is probably Farm and just reasoning from outside.

day.text: Two independent claims against one silent CAW-caller. Everyone on Gray.
day.note: Confident Gray is Meowfia. Call caw to end the day.

day.text: Alex claims Turkey and no visitors, yet my egg proves I visited. Alex is lying, and Alex is rushing CAW. Blair, Casey, Drew: throw at Alex.
day.note: Ellis and Alex are rushing to end the talk. Ellis's push on me looks suspicious now. Appeal to the rest of the table to look at Alex's impossible egg count.

day.text: The talk is nearly over.
Alex said "no eggs," not "no visitors" to Turkey. Finley clears Alex. Gray.
Gray's the cat. Everyone throw at Gray.
day.note: Gray is the likely Meowfia. Call the third CAW to end the day and go to the vote.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

review.title: The Pigeon Who Wasn't
review.headline: An honest Lazy Pigeon tells the truth, and the table eggsecutes him for it.
review.summary: Gray was a Lazy Pigeon who believed he was a Pigeon. He visited Alex, the Turkey, who stays home. So Alex got no egg and Gray got one from the Turkey. Both told the truth, but their stories seemed to clash. Ellis built a tidy case that Gray was a lying cat, and the table voted 6 to 1 against him. Blair, the only Meowfia, claimed Hawk, was never questioned, and took 18 points and the game.

rounds.recap: Drew, Ellis and Casey quickly backed each other up, which cleared them. Gray's Pigeon claim didn't fit with Alex's 'no eggs', and nobody thought of the Lazy Pigeon in the pool. Ellis paid an egg to extend the day and pushed hard on Gray, three CAWs ended the talk, and the honest Farm player Gray was eggsecuted. Blair's Meowfia won without ever being looked at.

highlights.text: Gray's private notes show him honestly confused: he knows he's the Pigeon, so he decides Alex or Finley must be lying.
Ellis spends his Wild to extend the day under Mulberry and uses the time to build a confident, logical and wrong case against Gray.
Gray asks the right question, 'Then where did my egg come from?', but nobody connects it to the Lazy Pigeon.
Blair the Maine Coon gives a Hawk claim that nobody can check, says almost nothing else, and wins alone with 18.

confusions.what: Said 'got no eggs, so no one visited me' as Turkey. A Turkey gains nothing from visitors; it gives them eggs. So a 0 count says nothing about who visited.

Threw everything thinking 'if we lose, my highest card comes back.' The consolation only applies if you threw at the other team. If Gray turned out Farm, Drew had thrown at his own team and got nothing back.
Argued that a Pigeon visit 'would've given Alex an egg', forgetting that the Lazy Pigeon is in the pool, sees itself as a Pigeon, and lays nothing when its target stays home.
Restated Alex's claim as 'Turkey and no visitors' and treated Alex's 0 eggs as proof Alex lied. A Turkey's own count doesn't change from visitors.
Called CAW CAW in speech and then again. It's unclear if the first call counted, since the clock had just been reset by the extension.

worked: Lazy Pigeon + Turkey created a real puzzle with a clear answer: Pigeon claim, +1 for Gray, 0 for Alex adds up only if Gray is a Lazy Pigeon. It was solvable and the table missed it, which is a good kind of failure.
Mulberry: Ellis paying his 0-value Wild to buy more talk was a real, cheap but meaningful decision, and it changed the outcome.
Public throw counts with hidden values: Gray throwing only 3 cards against everyone else's 4-5 was readable information.
Eagle/Falcon/Tit cross-checks let three players clear each other fast and gave the day a solid base to argue from.
problems: A one-round game makes the scoring meaningless. Whoever is Meowfia on a 1-Meowfia roll nearly wins by default, and the score announcements and the 'outscore your teammates' tension never come up. Play 3+ rounds.
Maine Coon's bet never came close to being used. Guessing all 7 animals from a 20-animal pool is close to impossible. Let it guess fewer players (e.g., 3), or reward partial guesses.
Crimson Kunzea was never used. It has to be done before your first message, which is too early to know anything. Allow it any time before you've accused someone, or before the CAW opens.

Chocolate Lily had no effect: no one claimed a hand size, and the log printed exact nest sizes at the start of the day. Check whether those were shown to players. If so, it's a bug against both the Lily and the base rule that nest sizes are hidden.

With 20 animals in the pool, players couldn't keep track of the odd roles (Lazy Pigeon, Galah, Magpie) that explain strange egg counts. Show a short pool summary during the day, or use a smaller pool.
